'''''Urera baccifera''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Urticaceae|nettle family]] known by many common names, including '''scratchbush''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=URBA|taxon=Urera baccifera|access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> '''''ortiga brava''''', '''''pringamoza''''', '''''mala mujer''''', '''''chichicaste''''', '''''nigua''''', '''''guaritoto''''', '''''ishanga''''', '''''manman guêpes''''', and '''''urtiga bronca'''''.<ref name=iitf>[http://www.fs.fed.us/global/iitf/Urera%20baccifera.pdf ''Urera baccifera''.] International Institute of Tropical Forestry.</ref> It is native to the Americas from Mexico through Central America into South America, as well as the Caribbean.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 19 January 2018}}</ref>

This species is a [[shrub]] or a small tree. It can reach five meters in height. The thin, toothed leaves are up to 25 centimeters long by 12.5 wide. The blades are borne on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The plant is covered in spines and stinging hairs. The inflorescence is a pink or purple cluster of flowers, and the plant is [[plant sexuality|dioecious]], with male and female parts on different plants. The spongy, juicy fruit is green or pinkish. The seeds are [[seed dispersal|dispersed]] by fruit-eating birds<ref name=iitf/> and [[Cebus apella|capuchin monkeys]].<ref name=dutra>Dutra, H. P., et al. (2006). [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1365-2435.2006.01096.x/pdf Dual ant attraction in the Neotropical shrub ''Urera baccifera'' (Urticaceae): the role of ant visitation to pearl bodies and fruits in herbivore deterrence and leaf longevity.] ''Functional Ecology'' 20 252-60.</ref>

[[File:Urera baccifera inflorescence.jpg|thumb|left|inflorescence]]

This plant grows in moist tropical forests. It is not very tolerant of shade, so it dies back when the [[overstory]] closes. It can be found in forests recently disturbed by fire.<ref name=iitf/>

In some areas, this plant is one of the first to bear fruit after the damage of a hurricane, and then it becomes an important food source for birds.<ref name=iitf/> The fruits also provide food for many species of [[ant]]. The ants also collect [[pearl body|pearl bodies]] which form on the leaves, stems, and stalks of the plant. Ants performing this activity include species in genera such as ''[[Camponotus]]'', ''[[Pheidole]]'', ''[[Crematogaster]]'', and ''[[Pseudomyrmex]]''. When ants are present on a plant, they rid it of [[lepidopteran]] larvae which would feed upon it, such as ''[[Smyrna blomfildia]]'', ''[[Urbanus esmeraldus]]'', and ''[[Pleuroptya silicalis]]''. This provides a benefit for both plant and ant in a [[mutualism (biology)|mutualistic]] relationship.<ref name=dutra/>
